hints: Identify all three forces acting on the particle: the weight $0.2g = 2\text{ N}$ acting vertically downwards, the tension $T$ directed along the string at $30^\circ$ to the wall, and the force $X$ perpendicular to the string.
Resolve forces along the string and perpendicular to the string to decouple the equations for $T$ and $X$.
Alternatively, resolve horizontally ($X \cos 30^\circ - T \sin 30^\circ = 0$) and vertically ($X \sin 30^\circ + T \cos 30^\circ - 2 = 0$), then solve simultaneously.
walkthrough:
Resolve forces parallel to the string in equilibrium:
$$T - 0.2g \cos 30^\circ = 0 \implies T = 2 \cos 30^\circ = 2 \times \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} = \sqrt{3} \approx 1.73\text{ N}$$

Resolve forces perpendicular to the string in equilibrium:
$$X - 0.2g \sin 30^\circ = 0 \implies X = 2 \sin 30^\circ = 2 \times \frac{1}{2} = 1\text{ N}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Draw or visualize the free-body diagram of the particle of mass $0.2\text{ kg}$. The three coplanar forces acting at the point are:
1. The downward weight $W = mg = 0.2 \times 10 = 2\text{ N}$.
2. The tension $T$ acting along the string towards the fixed support, making an angle of $30^\circ$ with the vertical wall.
3. The force of magnitude $X$, directed perpendicular to the string.

Choose axes aligned with the string: let the axis parallel to the string point upwards towards the wall, and the perpendicular axis point in the direction of $X$. Since $X$ is perpendicular to the string, it has zero component along the string, decoupling the equilibrium equations completely.

The angle between the downward vertical and the direction along the string is $30^\circ$. Therefore, the component of the weight along the string is $W \cos 30^\circ$, and the component perpendicular to the string is $W \sin 30^\circ$.

Set the net force parallel to the string equal to zero:
$$T - W \cos 30^\circ = 0$$
$$T = 2 \cos 30^\circ = 2\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) = \sqrt{3}\text{ N} \approx 1.732\text{ N} \approx 1.73\text{ N}$$

Set the net force perpendicular to the string equal to zero:
$$X - W \sin 30^\circ = 0$$
$$X = 2 \sin 30^\circ = 2\left(\frac{1}{2}\right) = 1\text{ N}$$
The tension in the string is $\sqrt{3}\text{ N} \approx 1.73\text{ N}$ and the magnitude of the force is $X = 1\text{ N}$.
